title: Modern computer vision from CNNs to foundation models: a unified framework for representation learning
title_zh: 从CNN到基础模型的现代计算机视觉：统一的表征学习框架
abstract: Abstract Modern computer vision is increasingly driven by the search for representations that generalize across tasks, modalities, and learning settings, rather than excelling at a single benchmark. This has produced a broad collection of architectures and paradigms, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), state-space models, foundation models, and diffusion-based generative models. Despite differing in design and training objectives, these approaches increasingly draw on a common set of principles: representation learning, self-attention, self-supervision, multimodal alignment, and generative modeling. As a result, the boundaries between discriminative, multimodal, and generative paradigms are becoming progressively less distinct. This survey examines that convergence through the lens of representation learning. We introduce a formal framework that classifies architectures by which component of an encoder–decoder pipeline they modify, unifies diverse training objectives as instances of a single alignment functional, and formalizes the locality–globality trade-off through two provable relationships linking a model’s locality, its computational cost, and the depth required to reach a global receptive field. Using this framework, we trace the evolution of vision architectures, from convolutional networks and Vision Transformers through hybrid and state-space designs to multimodal foundation models and modern generative frameworks, critically examining the limitations of each paradigm rather than reporting only their successes and complementing this analysis with a quantitative comparison across representative architectures. We show how discriminative, multimodal, and generative learning are converging around shared representational principles, argue for a unified representation-learning perspective on modern computer vision, and outline open challenges and concrete future directions toward general-purpose visual intelligence, multimodal foundation models, and trustworthy deployment.
abstract_zh: 摘要 现代计算机视觉越来越受到寻找能够跨任务、跨模态和跨学习环境泛化的表征驱动，而非仅在单一基准上表现出色。这产生了包括卷积神经网络（CNN）、视觉Transformer（ViT）、状态空间模型、基础模型和基于扩散的生成模型在内的广泛架构和范式。尽管在设计和训练目标上各异，但这些方法日益依赖一套共同的原则：表征学习、自注意力、自监督、多模态对齐和生成建模。因此，判别式、多模态和生成范式之间的界限变得越来越模糊。本综述通过表征学习的视角来考察这种收敛。我们引入一个对架构进行分类的正式框架，该框架根据编码器-解码器管线的哪个组件被修改来对架构进行分类，将多样化的训练目标统一为单一对齐函数的实例，并通过两个可证的关系 formalizes（形式化）了局部-全球权衡，这些关系将模型的局部性、其计算成本以及达到全局感受野所需的深度联系起来。利用该框架，我们追踪了视觉架构的演变，从卷积网络和视觉Transformer过渡到混合和状态空间设计，再到多模态基础模型和现代生成框架，批判性地审视每个范式的局限性，而不仅仅是报告其成功之处，并用代表性架构的定量比较补充此分析。我们展示了判别式、多模态和生成学习如何围绕共享的表征原则趋同，论证了对现代计算机视觉进行统一表征学习视角的必要性，并概述了朝向通用视觉智能、多模态基础模型和值得信赖部署的开放挑战和具体未来方向。
